accepted.title: Preventing monochromatic word concatenations across bounded gaps
accepted.text: Let X be any nonempty alphabet, finite or infinite, and let x=x_1x_2⋯ be an infinite word that is not eventually periodic. Let X* here denote its nonempty finite words. For a factor u of x, let A_x(u) be the first position where u occurs and B_x(u)=A_x(u)+|u|, the position just after that occurrence. Must there exist a finite colouring of X* for which no infinite sequence of factors (u_i) and finite integer C≥0 satisfy 0≤A_x(u_(i+1))−B_x(u_i)≤C for every i, while all concatenations u_(k_1)⋯u_(k_j), j≥1 and k_1<⋯<k_j, have one common colour?

accepted.title: A structural characterization of weak cop-win graphs
accepted.text: On a connected undirected loopless graph, the cop chooses a starting vertex, then the robber chooses one. They alternate moves, cop first, each moving to an adjacent vertex or staying put; capture occurs when they meet. Call the graph weak cop-win if the cop has a strategy guaranteeing capture or that the robber visits every vertex only finitely often. Characterize the graphs with this weak cop-win property in terms of their graph structure, allowing infinite graphs without a local-finiteness restriction.

accepted.title: Does finite-set evacuation imply local constructibility?
accepted.text: On a connected undirected loopless graph, the cop chooses a starting vertex, then the robber chooses one. They alternate moves, cop first, each moving to an adjacent vertex or staying put; capture occurs when they meet. Call the graph weak cop-win if the cop has a strategy guaranteeing capture or that the robber visits every vertex only finitely often. Suppose the cop has one strategy ensuring that, against every robber play and for every finite vertex set V, the robber leaves V at some time or is captured, with later return allowed. Must the graph be locally constructible: for every finite vertex set V, does some finite U⊇V have a constructible induced graph G[U]? A finite graph is constructible if it admits an order v_1,…,v_s such that, for each i>1, some earlier v_j has N[v_i]⊆N[v_j] within the induced graph on v_1,…,v_i, where N[v] is the closed neighbourhood.

Separate finite-target strategies combine on any connected graph by maintaining the finite set of robber vertices visited so far and walking to each required cop start; every uncaptured stage adds a new visited vertex. No countability assumption or enumeration of all finite sets is needed.

accepted.title: Arbitrarily delayed repeated returns in a weak cop-win graph
accepted.text: On a connected undirected loopless graph, the cop chooses a starting vertex, then the robber chooses one. They alternate moves, cop first, each moving to an adjacent vertex or staying put; capture occurs when they meet. Call the graph weak cop-win if the cop has a strategy guaranteeing capture or that the robber visits every vertex only finitely often. Does there exist a weak cop-win graph such that, for every cop starting vertex, the robber can choose a starting vertex v with this property: for every pair of positive integers m,n, the robber has a strategy against every cop play that avoids capture and either stays within some finite vertex set forever or visits v at a time t≥m and again at a time s≥t+n? The robber strategy may depend on m,n.

accepted.title: The union-closed conjecture for horizontal and vertical three-tiles
accepted.text: For every n≥3 and every three-element R⊂Z/nZ, let F be the family of all unions of translates in (Z/nZ)² of R×{0} and {0}×R, including the empty union. Must some point belong to at least half the members of F? Equivalently, since F is invariant under all torus translations, is the average |S| over S∈F at least n²/2?
